messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: Route53 latency spike observed for eu-west-1 edge endpoints (threshold 250ms) — 75% of checks failing. Rollup: service impact to inference-hosted API (higher latencies, occasional 5xxs).

kai_sre: I'm on it. beginning triage. linking handoff to oncall rota. @ada_ops can you grab customer-facing comms?

ada_ops: on it. Drafting status page blurb now. No incidents page yet until we know blast radius.

kai_sre: quick signal checks — CloudWatch shows Route53 resolver latency up from ~30ms -> 700ms for queries hitting eu-west-1. ELB health checks in azc (eu-west-1c) started failing ~2m after the dns spike.

ryan_prod: seeing increased 502s from api-gw -> inference-frontend in eu-west-1c. Other AZs look okay. Is cross-AZ egress healthy?

kai_sre: testing from jump box: `dig +trace api.redwood.local @8.8.8.8` shows some NS sets returning late answers; traceroute to edge proxy IPs times out at AWS peering hop in eu-west-1c.

jade_support: customers are opening tickets about slow responses. Tagged high priority.

kai_sre: hypothesis: regional edge route flap (peering path) causing intermittent DNS resolver timeouts which cascade to ELB health checks. Steps: 1) route traffic away from eu-west-1c via weighted failover 2) scale up instances in eu-west-1a/b 3) contact AWS support and open a networking case 4) document mitigation for postmortem.

ada_ops: approved. Publishing minimal status update: "We are investigating increased latency and errors for eu-west-1. Engineers are working on failover. No data loss expected." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

kai_sre: executing weighted DNS change (Route53):
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZABCDEFG --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.com.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-1c-proxy-avoid","Weight":0,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"203.0.113.10"}]}}]}'
```

kai_sre: also lowering ELB deregistration delay to 10s for quick drain in eu-west-1c target groups. running: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=10`

ryan_prod: scaling eu-west-1a/b pool +20% now. autoscaling policy bumped. Keep me posted if we need to redirect additional routes.

aws_service_bot: Support case created with AWS. Case ID: 1234567890. Initial reply ETA 15-30m. Investigating control plane and peering in eu-west-1.

kai_sre: telemetry after DNS weight flip: client-side retries dropped 60%, API latency 99p dropped from 1.2s -> 420ms. 5xx rate trending down but still elevated (0.8% -> 0.2%).

jade_support: customer comms updated with workaround note and request to avoid heavy batch jobs in eu-west-1 for next 2 hours.

ada_ops: handing off to night oncall @ryan_prod for follow-up, will maintain status page for the next hour. Kai — can you stay in watch for AWS updates?

kai_sre: staying. ping me if anything flips back. I'm collecting debug artifacts: `tcpdump` captures, dig logs, ELB access logs for postmortem.

ryan_prod: oncall ack. I'll monitor alarms and keep rotations informed. If AWS confirms peering, we'll leave DNS weight change in place for 2 hours then gradually shift traffic back.

aws_service_bot: AWS update: "We have observed an edge peering degradation impacting resolver performance in eu-west-1c. Network team applying mitigation; further updates in 20m."

kai_sre: copying key logs to incident channel and S3: `s3://redwood-incidents/2398765432/` — saved dig-trace.txt, elb-logs.tar.gz, tcpdump.pcap.

jade_support: received confirmation from 3 paying customers that perf improved after failover. marking as mitigated for them.

ada_ops: status page update pushed: "Mitigation in progress. Traffic redirected away from impacted AZ. Some users may still see elevated latency; we expect resolution within 2 hours." :white_check_mark:

ryan_prod: AWS just posted that peering routes are converging. Let's start rolling traffic back slowly — change weight eu-west-1c -> 20% then 50% over 30m if no regression.

kai_sre: rolling weights: `Weight eu-west-1c = 20` applied. Monitoring.

kai_sre: check: after bump to 20% we see a small blip in 5xx to 0.6% but settles within 3m. moving to 50%.

ryan_prod: raising to 50% now. No sustained regressions.

aws_service_bot: AWS final: "Control plane stabilization confirmed. Root cause: transient edge peering flap during maintenance event. No customers were impacted by data loss. We recommend reaching out if you need a detailed RCA."

ada_ops: updating final status: "Service degraded in eu-west-1 due to third-party (AWS) peering issue. Traffic was redirected and service restored. No data loss. Postmortem underway."

kai_sre: collecting timeline and impact numbers for postmortem. Will include: query latency graphs, ELB healthcheck failures by AZ, customer ticket IDs.

jade_support: closing customer-facing incident once postmortem is published.

ryan_prod: handoff note for next shift: monitor Route53 resolver latency, ELB unhealthy hosts in eu-west-1c, and AWS case 1234567890 for any follow-ups.

kai_sre: thanks team. Incident marked mitigated at 2398765745. Postmortem draft ETA 24h. :memo:
